description:
Problem: module- and session-scoped fixtures can change process state that the per-test checks never see, because those checks take their baseline after module fixtures run. _restore_logging_state (tests/conftest.py:390-401) silently restores root and benchbox.* loggers to that baseline, and _hermetic_state (tests/utilities/leak_detector.py:166-173) compares the quiet flag and other registered globals only per test and only for unit tests. A module fixture that changes them therefore contaminates every later module in the worker, and failures show up only under some worker placements. INC-15: the module-scoped contracts fixture in tests/unit/scripts/test_doc_contracts.py (:37-39 at c962e3e8733e9107988ba05145d09a27717a8fda, the parent of #3385) built MCP servers that left the benchbox logger at ERROR, and a later module's warning assertion failed on Trunk. INC-16: chDB sessions held open across modules, now caught by the module guard #3423 added (tests/conftest.py:378-387).

Outcome: an autouse module-scoped guard, built by extending tests/utilities/leak_detector.py (its snapshot, detect-and-restore and fail-with-restore reporting) rather than a second convention in conftest. It snapshots at module start and fails the module at its end when any of these changed: level, handlers, filters, propagate or disabled of the root logger and of every benchbox.* logger; filters on mcp.server.transport_security; benchbox.utils.printing._QUIET; the OpenTelemetry global tracer provider. It names each leaked item and restores what can be restored, so the next module starts clean. It never imports a module that is not already loaded.

Sequencing: lands after mcp-create-server-process-globals-20261025. On develop 121f24c2a three module fixtures leak the benchbox logger through create_server() (tests/unit/mcp/test_mcp_low_disk_guard.py:21-31, test_mcp_statistics_phase.py:22-36, test_mcp_tool_handlers.py:21-34). Once construction stops mutating globals they stop leaking, so this change does not add save-and-restore wrappers that the next change would delete.

Out of scope, with reason: shared output roots between xdist workers (#3442). That is filesystem sharing between processes, which a module-boundary state check cannot observe. It is pinned by tests/unit/test_session_isolation.py:249, and per-test environment changes are already caught by leak_detector.py:112-123.

Decision gates and stop conditions:
1. If the guard flags more than five existing modules, or a leak whose fix needs a production code change, stop and report the list instead of widening the change.
2. Reading the tracer provider must not create one (the OpenTelemetry API can build a provider from OTEL_PYTHON_TRACER_PROVIDER on first read). Check it only when opentelemetry.trace is already loaded, without side effects, and record how.
3. Never relax or silence a detection to make a module pass; fix the fixture.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests. No explanatory comments or docstrings in code; commits and PR bodies carry no tracker item IDs or session labels; any timing uses benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time().
